verdict.rationale: Runpod documents a first-party agent skills plugin. With it, users can ask their coding agent to create Pods, deploy Serverless endpoints, transfer files, or deploy code with Flash 'all in natural language.' It also documents two official MCP servers that connect AI tools and coding agents to Runpod. This natural-language control only works through an external coding agent plus Runpod's plugin or MCP server, not a built-in natural-language interface. The documented scope is limited to the listed operations. missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language interface, documentation that natural language covers all operations (e.g. billing, clusters, volumes), independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language commands work reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Once installed, you can ask your agent to create Pods, deploy Serverless endpoints, transfer files, or deploy your own code with Flash, all in natural language.
Runpod provides two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that connect AI tools and coding agents directly to Runpod
To migrate automatically, ask your coding agent to run `/runpod:migrate rest` once you've installed the Runpod skills plugin.
